written_by: the engineer, board 2 fix round, item B2-M4 (work/handoffs/phase-3/20261113_Board-2-Fix-Brief.md, call 4)
one_measure: total = bytes_as_placed + added_on_page + frame_bytes = the plate whole on the page, , UTF-8 bytes
how_measured: bytes_as_placed: the build report's weight.charts[specimen].bytes, the chart kit's figure HTML as guide_charts.py substitutes it into the page.
The figure was then found on the page () and measured: for 95 of the 97 chapter 14 charts it equals bytes_as_placed byte for byte.

added_on_page: what the build adds inside the figure after the report counts it: D2-975's <span class="nw"> round each atlas ID, 24 bytes each (S06 15 IDs, 360 bytes; S67 2 IDs, 48 bytes); 0 for every other chart.
frame_bytes: the plate whole less the figure as it sits on the page: the plate's head (label, size line), its scroll frame and stage, the alt paragraph where the plate has one, and its caption.
total: the plate whole, measured by script (nesting-aware, so a kit figure inside the plate is counted once).

For a rule plate (rules 14.1 to 14.14), frame_and_other_bytes is the plate less its charts, so it holds the plate's own HTML specimen as well as the frame. For a sketch, stage_bytes is the stage's inside as guide_charts.py measures it, and sketch_file_bytes the file on disk.
The kit's weight line (oa-chart.mjs build) estimates the frame at 750 bytes; this file measures each plate's own. S73's frame, for one, is 811.
